proofs.proof_tex:
Assume first that \(\alpha_n(3T+2\varepsilon)\le 1\), so that the exact-primitives proposition makes every \(p_{n,x,h}^\dagger\) a probability distribution and hence makes \(\nu_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger\) a genuine prior.  Conditional on \((X^\dagger,H^\dagger)=(x,h)\), the labeled response types are independent with common distribution \(p_{n,x,h}^\dagger\).  Indeed, if a labeled type sequence has count vector \(m\), then the multinomial-count probability times the reciprocal orbit size is
\[
 \left\{\frac{n!}{\prod_t m_t!}\prod_t
 \left(p_{n,x,h,t}^\dagger\right)^{m_t}\right\}
 \left\{\frac{\prod_t m_t!}{n!}\right\}
 =\prod_{i=1}^n p_{n,x,h,t_i}^\dagger.
\tag{1}
\]
This also verifies directly that the target under the prior remains the finite-population quantity \(n^{-1}\sum_i(c^\dagger)^\top t_i\), rather than its conditional prior mean.

Write \(\vartheta(t)=(c^\dagger)^\top t\).  The central types \(000\) and \(111\) have \(\vartheta(t)=0\).  The exact-primitives proposition gives
\[
 \sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^+\vartheta(t)^2
 =\sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^-\vartheta(t)^2=\frac58,
 \qquad
 \sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^+\vartheta(t)^2
 =\sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^-\vartheta(t)^2=\frac3{16}.
\tag{2}
\]
The equalities for the negative measures also follow by complementing every type, which changes \(\vartheta\) to \(-\vartheta\) and leaves its square unchanged.  Substituting the definition of \(p_{n,x,h}^\dagger\) and using the zero central contribution therefore gives the exact identity
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\vartheta(t_i)^2\mid x,h\right]
 =\alpha_n\left(\frac58|x|+\frac3{16}|h|\right).
\tag{3}
\]
The two specified polynomial densities satisfy
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E|X^\dagger|
 &=\frac{30}{16T}\int_0^T x\left(1-\frac{x^2}{T^2}\right)^2\,dx
 =\frac{5T}{16},\\
 \mathbb E|H^\dagger|
 &=\frac{30}{16\varepsilon}\int_0^\varepsilon h
 \left(1-\frac{h^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right)^2\,dh
 =\frac{5\varepsilon}{16}.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]

Now use independent assignment with probabilities \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\), and define the observable Horvitz--Thompson summand, its unprojected average, and its admissible clipped version by
\[
 Z_i=\frac{c_{A_i}^\dagger\{Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1/2\}}
 {q_{A_i}^\dagger},
 \qquad
 \overline\tau_{\mathrm{HT}}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i,
 \qquad
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{HT}}=\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}
 (\overline\tau_{\mathrm{HT}}).
\tag{5}
\]
Every denominator in (5) is positive.  For each fixed schedule, the zero-sum contrast condition and \(q_a^\dagger=|c_a^\dagger|/2\) imply
\[
 \mathbb E_A Z_i=(c^\dagger)^\top Y_i=\vartheta(t_i),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_A Z_i^2
 =\sum_{a=1}^3\frac{(c_a^\dagger)^2}{4q_a^\dagger}
 =\frac12\sum_{a=1}^3|c_a^\dagger|=1.
\tag{6}
\]
Independence of the assignments across units and (6) yield the exact conditional randomization risk
\[
 \mathbb E_A\!\left[
 \{\overline\tau_{\mathrm{HT}}-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2
 \mid y\right]
 =\frac1{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^n\{1-\vartheta(t_i)^2\}.
\tag{7}
\]
Averaging (7) under the genuine tube prior, and then applying (3)--(4) and \(\alpha_n=n^{-1/3}\), gives
\[
 \operatorname{BayesRisk}(\overline\tau_{\mathrm{HT}})
 =\frac1n-n^{-4/3}\left(\frac{25T}{128}
 +\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}\right).
\tag{8}
\]

The normalization of \(c^\dagger\) puts every target value in \([-1,1]\), so clipping cannot increase squared error.  Let \(\pi\) be the allocation-count law under this independent design.  Conditional on \(r\), its assignment is uniform over all labeled assignments with that count vector.  By the exact posterior square-completion calculation, \(\mathcal B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger(r)\) is the minimum conditional Bayes risk in that experiment.  Hence the posterior-mean rule is no worse than the admissible clipped rule in (5), whose risk is no larger than (8), and
\[
 B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger
 \le \sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\pi(r)
 \mathcal B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger(r)
 \le \frac1n-n^{-4/3}\left(\frac{25T}{128}
 +\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}\right).
\tag{9}
\]
The first inequality in (9) is the elementary fact that a minimum is at most a convex average.  By the definitions of \(B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger\) and \(G_n(r)\), (9) is equivalent to
\[
 \max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}G_n(r)
 =n^{4/3}\left\{\frac1n-B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger\right\}
 \ge \frac{25T}{128}+\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}.
\tag{10}
\]

For the prescribed schedule, \(T_n\le n^{1/12}\), \(T_n\to\infty\), and \(\varepsilon_n=T_n^{-1}\).  Therefore
\[
 \alpha_n(3T_n+2\varepsilon_n)
 \le 3n^{-1/4}+2n^{-1/3}\longrightarrow0,
\tag{11}
\]
so the positivity condition holds for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Equations (10)--(11) then imply
\[
 \max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}G_n(r)
 \ge \frac{25T_n}{128}+\frac{15}{256T_n}
 \longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{12}
\]

Finally, the local and shell conclusions in the original claim would imply the opposite.  On \(\mathcal F_n(M_n)\), multiplying the proposed local remainder bound by \(n^{4/3}\) gives
\(G_n(r)\le J_{\varepsilon_n,T_n}^\star+
\Omega_{\varepsilon_n,T_n,M_n}^\dagger(n)\).  On every exterior shell or zero-count face, outwardness of \(\overline G\) and \(\underline J^\star\), together with the definition of \(\Delta_{\mathrm{shell}}^\dagger\), gives
\(G_n(r)\le J_{\varepsilon_n,T_n}^\star+
\Delta_{\mathrm{shell}}^\dagger(n,M_n)\).  Those sets partition \(\mathcal R_{n,3}\), whence
\[
 \max_rG_n(r)\le J_{\varepsilon_n,T_n}^\star+
 \max\!\left\{
 \Omega_{\varepsilon_n,T_n,M_n}^\dagger(n),
 \Delta_{\mathrm{shell}}^\dagger(n,M_n)\right\}.
\tag{13}
\]
The claimed tube-removal bound and the three claimed vanishing moduli would make the right side of (13) converge to the finite number \(\mathfrak L^\dagger\), contradicting (12).  Thus (10) is an exact early-kill certificate: the widening polynomial density \(w_T\) cannot support the asserted finite tube-removal limit.

Fix inputs satisfying the displayed positivity condition.  The established algebraic-certificate theorem applies with exactly \((n,T,\varepsilon,\delta)\) and returns rational endpoints \(B^-_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}\) and \(B^+_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}\) after a number of bit operations polynomial in the displayed input length.  It proves
\[
 B^-_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}
 \le B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger
 \le B^+_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta},
 \qquad
 B^+_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}-B^-_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}
 \le\delta.
\tag{16}
\]
For any outcome-independent design and estimator, its maximum risk over schedules is at least its Bayes risk under the genuine tube prior.  The permutation-orbit Bayes lemma bounds that Bayes risk below by \(B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger\).  Taking the infimum over designs and estimators in the risk-game definition gives
\[
 R_n(c^\dagger)\ge B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger
 \ge B^-_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}.
\tag{17}
\]
Subtracting (17) from \(n^{-1}\) and multiplying by the positive number \(n^{4/3}\) gives the final finite-sample deficit certificate.  Termination and the width claim come from the algebraic-certificate theorem; no cross-sample convergence assertion is used.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Assume that rational \(T\ge1\), rational \(\varepsilon>0\), and \(n\ge1\) satisfy \(\alpha_n(3T+2\varepsilon)\le1\). Let \(\pi\) be the allocation-count law induced by independent assignment with probabilities \(q^\dagger\). Then \[B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger\le\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\pi(r)\mathcal B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger(r)\le n^{-1}-n^{-4/3}\left(\frac{25T}{128}+\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}\right),\] and consequently \[\max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}G_n(r)\ge\frac{25T}{128}+\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}.\] Along \(T_n=2^{\lfloor(\log_2n)/12\rfloor}\) and \(\varepsilon_n=T_n^{-1}\), positivity holds eventually and \(\max_rG_n(r)\to\infty\). Hence there is no finite \(\mathfrak L^\dagger\) for which both \(J_{\varepsilon_n,T_n}^\star\to\mathfrak L^\dagger\) and \[\max_rG_n(r)\le J_{\varepsilon_n,T_n}^\star+\max\{\Omega_{\varepsilon_n,T_n,M_n}^\dagger(n),\Delta_{\mathrm{shell}}^\dagger(n,M_n)\}\] hold with the two displayed error terms tending to zero.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current conjunction is false for its stated widening polynomial prior. The exact Horvitz--Thompson calculation under the same prior forces the best fixed-count Bayes deficit to be at least \(25T/128+15\varepsilon/256\). Since \(T_n\to\infty\), this contradicts the claimed finite tube-removal limit and vanishing global allocation errors. The proposed claim records the exact generic-class certificate rather than assuming the missing coefficient expansion.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}\ge\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}>0.\] This one-sided attaining result does not assert existence of the limit or a matching all-design converse.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The claimed equality depends on the allocation-tube theorem, whose stated tube-removal schedule is contradicted by the exact diverging-deficit certificate. The uniform independent-design procedure still proves the displayed positive lower limit, but no frozen result supplies the reverse inequality.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Let \(n\ge1\), rational \(T\ge1\), rational \(\varepsilon>0\), and rational \(\delta>0\) satisfy \(\alpha_n(3T+2\varepsilon)\le1\). A deterministic Turing algorithm terminates and returns rationals \(B^-_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}\) and \(B^+_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}\) such that \[B^-_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}\le B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger\le B^+_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta},\qquad B^+_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}-B^-_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}\le\delta,\] with bit complexity polynomial in \(n\), the rational input lengths, and \(\log(1/\delta)\). Moreover, \[B^-_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}\le R_n(c^\dagger),\qquad n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}\le n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-B^-_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}\}.\] This is a same-input finite certificate and makes no cross-sample threshold claim.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Exact algebraic evaluation at a fixed admissible input is proved, as is the all-design Bayes comparison. The advertised cross-sample modulus is false for the prescribed widening tube because its exact deficit diverges at least linearly in \(T_n\); testing successive sample sizes cannot certify all later sizes.

proposed.statement: Assume that rational \(T\ge1\), rational \(\varepsilon>0\), and \(n\ge1\) satisfy \(\alpha_n(3T+2\varepsilon)\le1\). Let \(\pi\) be the allocation-count law induced by independent assignment with probabilities \(q^\dagger\). Then \[B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger\le\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\pi(r)\mathcal B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger(r)\le n^{-1}-n^{-4/3}\left(\frac{25T}{128}+\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}\right),\] and consequently \[\max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}G_n(r)\ge\frac{25T}{128}+\frac{15\varepsilon}{256}.\] Along \(T_n=2^{\lfloor(\log_2n)/12\rfloor}\) and \(\varepsilon_n=T_n^{-1}\), positivity holds eventually and \(\max_rG_n(r)\to\infty\). Hence there is no finite \(\mathfrak L^\dagger\) for which both \(J_{\varepsilon_n,T_n}^\star\to\mathfrak L^\dagger\) and \[\max_rG_n(r)\le J_{\varepsilon_n,T_n}^\star+\max\{\Omega_{\varepsilon_n,T_n,M_n}^\dagger(n),\Delta_{\mathrm{shell}}^\dagger(n,M_n)\}\] hold with the two displayed error terms tending to zero.
proposed.justification: This exact early-kill certificate tests the proposed full-dimensional prior against a legal independent design and exposes its unavoidable widening-tube deficit.
proposed.gap: The polynomial density scaled to \([-T,T]\) has \(\mathbb E|X^\dagger|=5T/16\), so its second-order variance-pressure term grows linearly rather than converging to a finite Airy value.
proposed.consumer: It prevents a prospective three-regimen precision calculation from using an invalid finite-to-limit certificate and isolates the need for a differently shaped least-favorable prior.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The corrected target uses the exact tube prior but removes the contradicted coefficient, shell-convergence, and primal-attainment assertions; its dependencies are the exact finite-prior nodes actually used by the proof.

proposed.statement: For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}\ge\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}>0.\] This one-sided attaining result does not assert existence of the limit or a matching all-design converse.
proposed.justification: This is the strongest established asymptotic statement at the unequal contrast after the proposed converse prior fails its exact early-kill test.
proposed.gap: Existence and identification of the unrestricted second-order limit remain open; the widening polynomial tube cannot prove them.
proposed.consumer: It supplies an attainable positive second-order precision benchmark, but not a sharp worst-case equality for trial planning.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed claim needs the established independent-design attaining theorem directly; the contradicted allocation-tube theorem is removed from its proof spine.

proposed.statement: Let \(n\ge1\), rational \(T\ge1\), rational \(\varepsilon>0\), and rational \(\delta>0\) satisfy \(\alpha_n(3T+2\varepsilon)\le1\). A deterministic Turing algorithm terminates and returns rationals \(B^-_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}\) and \(B^+_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}\) such that \[B^-_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}\le B_{n,\varepsilon,T}^\dagger\le B^+_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta},\qquad B^+_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}-B^-_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}\le\delta,\] with bit complexity polynomial in \(n\), the rational input lengths, and \(\log(1/\delta)\). Moreover, \[B^-_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}\le R_n(c^\dagger),\qquad n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}\le n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-B^-_{n,\varepsilon,T,\delta}\}.\] This is a same-input finite certificate and makes no cross-sample threshold claim.
proposed.justification: This retains the terminating exact-algebraic finite certificate that is actually proved at each admissible rational input.
proposed.gap: No computable threshold controls all later sample sizes because the prescribed widening tube has a diverging deficit.
proposed.consumer: A designer may certify a finite prior lower bound at a selected sample size, but may not infer the rejected sharp asymptotic modulus.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The dependency spine is replaced by the exact algebraic evaluator and the finite all-design Bayes comparison; the false cross-sample tube claims are removed.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}\ge C_A(5/8)^{2/3}>0\). For the stated polynomial tube, \(\max_rG_n(r)\ge25T_n/128+15/(256T_n)\to\infty\), so neither a matching unrestricted limit nor the advertised fixed finite-to-limit schedule is established.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The former metadata advertised a sharp equality and finite tube coefficient contradicted by the exact prior-averaged Horvitz--Thompson calculation.

proofs.proof_tex:
The already established theorem \(\mathrm{thm:qstar\text{-}uniform\text{-}risk\text{-}upper}\) proves that \(\delta_n^\star\) is total and supplies a finite \(B_c\) for which
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
\le\max_y\mathbb E[(\delta_n^\star-\tau_c(y))^2]
\le\frac1n-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+B_cn^{-3/2}.
\tag{19}
\]
The first inequality is the definition of the minimax infimum under the fixed independent design; all ratios in the procedure are supported because \(q_a^\star>0\) on \(S_c\), as proved in that theorem.

Conversely, \(\mathrm{lem:qstar\text{-}full\text{-}label\text{-}bayes\text{-}converse}\) shows that for every positive rational \(\eta\), eventually
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
\ge\frac1n-(\Lambda_c+\eta)n^{-4/3}.
\tag{20}
\]
Put
\[
e_n=n^{4/3}\left[R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
-\left\{n^{-1}-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}\right\}\right].
\]
Equations (19)--(20) give \(-\eta\le e_n\le B_cn^{-1/6}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Since this holds for every positive rational \(\eta\), one has \(e_n\to0\).  This is precisely
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
=\frac1n-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).
\]
Together with the first assertion of (19), this proves every clause of the theorem.

added_lemmas.statement:
For each fixed permitted contrast \(c\), consider the fixed design under which the assignments are independent with probabilities \(q^\star\).  For every positive rational \(\eta\), there is an integer \(N=N(c,\eta)\) such that, for every \(n\ge N\),
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
\ge \frac1n-\{\Lambda_c+\eta\}n^{-4/3}.
\]
The bound applies to every possibly randomized estimator using the complete assignment labels and observed outcomes.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(S=S_c\), \(s_a=\operatorname{sign}(c_a)\), \(q_a=|c_a|/2\) for \(a\in S\), and \(\kappa=\kappa(c)\).  The support assumption and the definition of \(S\) imply \(q_a>0\) on \(S\), while the normalization gives \(\sum_{a\in S}q_a=1\).  Inactive arms have design probability zero and will be assigned potential outcome zero in the prior below.

By the primal attainment assertion in \(\mathrm{lem:response\text{-}cost\text{-}geometry}\), choose a nonnegative measure \(\lambda^+\) on \(\mathcal T_c\) such that
\[
\sum_t\lambda_t^+b_t=v,
\qquad
\sum_t\lambda_t^+\theta_t^2=\kappa.
\]
Let \(M=\sum_t\lambda_t^+<\infty\), and define its complement by
\(\lambda_t^-=\lambda_{mathbf1-t}^+\).  Since
\(b_{mathbf1-t}=-b_t\) and, by the zero-sum assumption,
\(\theta_{mathbf1-t}=-\theta_t\),
\[
\sum_t\lambda_t^-b_t=-v,
\qquad
\sum_t\lambda_t^-\theta_t^2=\kappa,
\qquad
\sum_t\lambda_t^-=M.
\]
Put \(p_0=(\delta_{mathbf0}+\delta_{mathbf1})/2\).  Both atoms in \(p_0\) have \(\theta_t=0\).

Fix a positive rational \(\eta\).  From \(\mathrm{def:airy\text{-}benchmark}\), the normalized ground state \(\phi_c\) has finite energy
\[
4\int_{\mathbb R}|\phi_c'(x)|^2\,dx
+\kappa\int_{\mathbb R}|x|\phi_c(x)^2\,dx=\Lambda_c.
\]
Multiplying \(\phi_c\) by cutoffs that equal one on \([-T+1,T-1]\), then normalizing and smoothing inside \((-T,T)\), shows directly by dominated convergence and the product rule that there are a finite \(T\) and a nonnegative \(\varphi\in C_c^1((-T,T))\) such that
\[
\int\varphi^2=1,
\qquad
I_\varphi+\kappa m_\varphi\le\Lambda_c+\eta/2,
\qquad
I_\varphi=4\int|\varphi'|^2,quad
m_\varphi=\int|x|\varphi(x)^2\,dx.
\]
Indeed, the derivative of a cutoff contributes only on the tails, where both the \(H^1\) mass and the weighted \(L^2\) mass tend to zero; smoothing on the resulting compact interval preserves the two displayed integrals.  Thus no normalized full-dimensional ground state is being used.

Set \(\alpha=n^{-1/3}\) and let \(X\) have density
\(\pi(x)=\varphi(x)^2\).  For \(x\ge0\) and \(x<0\), respectively, define the response-type laws
\[
p_{n,x}=(1-\alpha|x|M)p_0+\alpha|x|\lambda^+,
\qquad
p_{n,x}=(1-\alpha|x|M)p_0+\alpha|x|\lambda^-.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\alpha TM\le1\), so these are probability measures; this is the only positivity condition needed for the prior.  Conditional on \(X=x\), draw the active response types \(T_1,\ldots,T_n\) independently from \(p_{n,x}\), extend each type by zero on inactive arms, and then draw the assignments independently from \(q\), independently of the types.  Integrating out \(X\) gives a genuine prior on the finite set of complete binary schedules, fixed independently of the randomization design.

For \(\Theta_i=c^\top b_{T_i}\), the preceding moment identities and \(c^\top v=1\) give exactly
\[
\mathbb E(\Theta_i\mid X=x)=\alpha x,
\qquad
\mathbb E(\Theta_i^2\mid X=x)=\alpha\kappa|x|.
\tag{1}
\]
Because \(\mathbf1^\top c=0\), the realized finite-population estimand under this prior is not replaced by a prior mean: it is exactly
\[
H_n:=\tau_c(y)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\Theta_i.
\tag{2}
\]

On every positive-probability observation define
\[
Z_i=s_{A_i}(2Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1)\in\{-1,1\},
\qquad \overline Z_n=n^{-1}\sum_iZ_i,
\qquad p=\alpha X.
\]
For each \(a\in S\), the first identity in (1) at the vector level yields
\[
\mathbb E\{s_a(2T_{i,a}-1)\mid X=x\}
=2s_a\alpha x v_a=\alpha x.
\]
Consequently the full one-unit observation \(O_i=(A_i,Z_i)\) satisfies
\[
\Pr(O_i=(a,z)\mid X=x)=q_a\frac{1+pz}{2}.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus the assignment labels are ancillary for \(X\), but they have not been discarded from estimation of the realized target \(H_n\).  Conditional on \(X\), the \(Z_i\) are independent Rademacher variables with mean \(p\).

Let \(\mathscr Z_n=\sigma(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)\) and
\(\mu_n=\mathbb E(p\mid\mathscr Z_n)\).  We first calculate the scalar Bayes risk for \(p\).  Define
\[
\rho(x)=\frac{\pi'(x)}{\pi(x)}=\frac{2\varphi'(x)}{\varphi(x)}
\quad\hbox{when }\varphi(x)>0,
\]
and set it to zero on the null set where \(\varphi=0\).  Then
\[
\mathbb E\rho(X)^2=4\int|\varphi'(x)|^2\,dx=I_\varphi.
\tag{4}
\]
For each realized \(Z_1,ldots,Z_n\), integration by parts in \(x\) has no boundary term because \(\pi\) is compactly supported and vanishes at its boundary.  Since
\[
\frac{z}{1+pz}=\frac{z-p}{1-p^2},\qquad z\in\{-1,1\},
\]
the posterior score identity is
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[
\rho(X)+n\alpha\frac{\overline Z_n-p}{1-p^2}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr Z_n\right]=0.
\tag{5}
\]
The division is valid for all sufficiently large \(n\), because
\(|p|\le\alpha T<1/2\).

Let \(G_n=\mathbb E\{\rho(X)\mid\mathscr Z_n\}\).  From (5),
\[
n\alpha(\overline Z_n-\mu_n)=-G_n-E_n,
\quad
E_n=n\alpha\,\mathbb E\!\left[
\frac{p^2(\overline Z_n-p)}{1-p^2}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr Z_n\right].
\tag{6}
\]
Conditional Jensen's inequality, followed by
\(\mathbb E\{(\overline Z_n-p)^2\mid X\}=(1-p^2)/n\), gives
\[
\mathbb E E_n^2
\le n^2\alpha^2\mathbb E\!\left[
\frac{p^4(\overline Z_n-p)^2}{(1-p^2)^2}\right]
=n\alpha^2\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{p^4}{1-p^2}\right]
\le C_T n\alpha^6=O(n^{-1}).
\tag{7}
\]

It remains to identify the limit of \(G_n\) without assuming a limit experiment.  Put
\(\widehat X_n=\operatorname{proj}_{[-T,T]}(\overline Z_n/\alpha)\).  Since projection cannot increase distance from \(X\in[-T,T]\),
\[
\mathbb E(\widehat X_n-X)^2
\le\alpha^{-2}\mathbb E(\overline Z_n-p)^2
\le(n\alpha^2)^{-1}=n^{-1/3}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{8}
\]
For any bounded continuous \(f\) on \([-T,T]\), (8) and uniform continuity imply \(f(\widehat X_n)\to f(X)\) in \(L^2\).  Approximating the \(L^2(\pi)\) function \(\rho\) by such functions and using that conditional expectation is the \(L^2\) projection onto \(\mathscr Z_n\) gives
\[
\mathbb E\{\rho(X)-G_n\}^2\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
\mathbb EG_n^2\longrightarrow I_\varphi.
\tag{9}
\]
Equations (6)--(9) imply
\[
n^2\alpha^2\mathbb E(\overline Z_n-\mu_n)^2\longrightarrow I_\varphi.
\tag{10}
\]
The conditional-mean projection identity and the conditional variance of \(\overline Z_n\) now give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E(p-\mu_n)^2
&=\mathbb E(\overline Z_n-p)^2
-\mathbb E(\overline Z_n-\mu_n)^2\\
&=\frac1n-I_\varphi n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
because \(\mathbb E(p^2)/n=O(n^{-5/3})\).

We next pass from the latent mean \(p\) to the actual finite-population target (2).  Write \(W_n=H_n-p\), let \(\mathscr O_n=\sigma(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), and put
\(\zeta_n=\mathbb E(H_n\mid\mathscr O_n)\).  For a one-unit observation \(o\), define
\[
d_x(o)=\mathbb E(\Theta_i-p\mid X=x,O_i=o).
\]
At \(p_0\), \(\Theta_i=0\).  The total variation of
\(p_{n,x}-p_0\) is bounded by a constant times \(\alpha|x|\), and (3) bounds every conditional binary-outcome denominator below by \(1/4\) once \(\alpha T<1/2\).  Hence, for a finite constant depending only on the fixed contrast and the fixed \(\eta\)-dependent prior,
\[
|d_x(o)|\le C_{c,\eta}\alpha|x|.
\tag{12}
\]
Also \(\mathbb E\{d_x(O_i)\mid X=x\}=0\).  Conditional on \((X,O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), the response types remain independent across units, so conditional Jensen and (12) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E(\zeta_n-\mu_n)^2
&=\mathbb E\!\left[\mathbb E(W_n\mid\mathscr O_n)^2\right]\\
&\le\mathbb E\!\left[\mathbb E(W_n\mid X,\mathscr O_n)^2\right]
=\frac1n\mathbb E\{d_X(O_1)^2\}
\le C_{c,\eta}\frac{\alpha^2}{n}=O(n^{-5/3}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
\]
Here \(\mu_n=\mathbb E(p\mid\mathscr O_n)\) as well, by the ancillarity in (3).

The remaining covariance is exact.  Conditional on a response type \(t\),
\[
\mathbb E(Z_i\mid T_i=t)
=\sum_{a\in S}\frac{|c_a|}{2}s_a(2t_a-1)
=\sum_{a\in S}c_at_a-\frac12\sum_{a\in S}c_a
=\theta_t.
\tag{14}
\]
Therefore, using independence across units conditional on \(X\),
\[
\mathbb E\{(p-\overline Z_n)W_n\mid X\}
=-\frac1n\operatorname{Var}(\Theta_i\mid X)
=-\mathbb E(W_n^2\mid X).
\tag{15}
\]
Moreover, (10), (13), and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
\left|\mathbb E\{(\overline Z_n-\mu_n)W_n\}\right|
=\left|\mathbb E\{(\overline Z_n-\mu_n)(\zeta_n-\mu_n)\}\right|
=O(n^{-3/2})=o(n^{-4/3}).
\tag{16}
\]
Combining (1), (11), and (15)--(16),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E(H_n-\mu_n)^2
&=\mathbb E(p-\mu_n)^2+\mathbb EW_n^2
+2\mathbb E\{(p-\mu_n)W_n\}\\
&=\mathbb E(p-\mu_n)^2-\mathbb EW_n^2+o(n^{-4/3})\\
&=\frac1n-\{I_\varphi+\kappa m_\varphi\}n^{-4/3}
+o(n^{-4/3}),
\end{aligned}
\tag{17}
\]
because
\[
\mathbb EW_n^2
=\frac1n\mathbb E\{\alpha\kappa|X|-\alpha^2X^2\}
=\kappa m_\varphi n^{-4/3}+O(n^{-5/3}).
\]
Finally, posterior square completion and (13) show that the Bayes risk for the realized causal target is
\[
\mathcal B_n
:=\mathbb E(H_n-\zeta_n)^2
=\mathbb E(H_n-\mu_n)^2-\mathbb E(\zeta_n-\mu_n)^2
=\frac1n-\{I_\varphi+\kappa m_\varphi\}n^{-4/3}
+o(n^{-4/3}).
\tag{18}
\]
This calculation retains the full labels.  In particular, their finite-sample improvement over a scalar-only posterior is represented by the nonnegative term in (13), which is \(O(n^{-5/3})\) and therefore does not alter (18).

As the requested unequal-three-arm stress check, when
\(c=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), one may take
\[
\lambda^+=\delta_{000}+\delta_{101}+\delta_{110},
\qquad M=3,
\qquad q=(1/2,1/8,3/8).
\]
Direct enumeration gives
\[
\sum_t\lambda_t^+b_t=(1/2,-1/2,-1/2)=v,
\qquad
\sum_t\lambda_t^+\theta_t^2=0+(1/4)^2+(3/4)^2=5/8.
\]
For every one of the eight response types, (14) holds exactly.  Hence all three transformed arm observations in (3) have the same slope \(\alpha x\), while the full label remains present in \(d_x(O_i)\).  The product calculation is unconditional over every assignment vector, including realized allocations with a zero arm count, and divides only by \(1-p^2\ge3/4\), never by a realized count.  Thus the fixed-design boundary allocations and the known finite-sample usefulness of labels are not removed by a sufficiency assumption; the latter is controlled by (13) only at the order needed here.

For every estimator, its maximum risk over fixed schedules is at least its average risk under the constructed schedule prior, and conditional Jensen shows that estimator randomization cannot lower the posterior squared-error risk below \(\mathcal B_n\).  Taking the infimum over all full-label estimators therefore gives
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)\ge\mathcal B_n.
\]
The energy choice gives
\(I_\varphi+\kappa m_\varphi\le\Lambda_c+\eta/2\); after increasing \(N(c,\eta)\), the remainder in (18) is bounded below by \(-\eta n^{-4/3}/2\).  Hence, for every \(n\ge N(c,\eta)\),
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
\ge\frac1n-(\Lambda_c+\eta)n^{-4/3},
\]
which proves the lemma.

proposed.statement:
For every fixed permitted \(c\), the estimator \(\delta_n^\star\) is total and there is a finite \(B_c\) such that
\[
\max_y\mathbb E[(\delta_n^\star-\tau_c(y))^2]\le\frac1n-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+B_cn^{-3/2}.
\]
In addition, the minimax risk under the fixed independent design has the sharp expansion
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)=\frac1n-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).
\]
proposed.justification: It converts the dual score and Airy feedback into a full-label finite-data procedure and fixes the restricted benchmark sharply.
proposed.gap: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen prove this shape only for two arms; Hull's Theorem 1 has the same two-arm restriction and no multiarm second-order coefficient.
proposed.consumer: A trialist can implement this prespecified procedure as a restricted benchmark without treating it as a claim about unrestricted design optimality.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof now uses the already established uniform attaining theorem and the new full-label Bayes-converse lemma, so both dependencies must be explicit.
